record_notes.DCP-LETT-1756: September 27, 1855. Crowe sends two beans through an English traveller to the Royal Society, obtained through Blytt, from Vaeroe/Lofoten and Alten/Finmark. Explicitly not in pods; Gulf Stream transport is prevailing opinion, not witnessed transit. Requests their names on Blytt behalf and promises any additional specimens. Darwin later annotations supply names, distinguish collection locations and state ten-day flotation; they are undated and cannot be treated as Crowe September text or same-day Darwin knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1777: November 9, 1855. Explicitly answers Crowe seed shipment and naming request. Seeds arrived some time earlier, floated in Darwin ten-day test and were planted at Kew, but he has not heard whether they germinated. Distinguish experiment endpoints. Supplies Entada scandens and Mucuna urens names with distribution and nicknames, and requests only different kinds in future. P4 reports carrying a message to Sabine that does not occur in 1756; hold that paragraph as missing-input grounding. No exact physical receipt date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1790: December 5, 1855 signed Benson memorandum, main P1–14 fully read. Addressed content is supported by metadata recipient Darwin and P11 your requirements, though no salutation or covering letter survives. Distinguishes observed specimens, other collectors reports, doubtful localities, suspected synonyms and uncertain elevations across Cyclophorus, Pterocyclus, Achatina, Helix, Bulimus and Pupa. Ceylon/India locality claims are often qualified; preserve uncertainty and damaged-word marks. Bulimus Bengalensis discontinuous distribution and Madeira/St Helena shell identity are explicitly answered in 4354. Darwin annotations and later Natural selection use are separate and undated here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-4354: December 7, supplied 1855, surviving copy of Darwin letter. P1–3 specifically thanks for facts and answers Benson memorandum on shell ranges, Madeira/St Helena and Bulimus Bengalensis, adds a conditional offer to find remaining St Helena shells and asks about freshwater range. P4 promise to keep future enquiries in mind and P5–7 health/water-cure reply require a missing covering note; those inputs are absent from 1790. Restrict response pair to P1–3. Authorship is Darwin but carrier is a copy, not original autograph. No later Benson reply found in apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13784: Conjectured March 20, 1855, based on Tuesday heading, diary and later conversation note. Thanks a missing Bunbury note and proposes Saturday morning talk before departure. Redirecting to Mrs Bunbury is a delivery arrangement, not evidence that she wrote the body or that the meeting already occurred. Footnote describes March 25 notes on flora; these are separate later witnesses. April 10 incoming 1664 answers a different missing letter of scientific questions, not this visit arrangement.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1664: April 10, 1855 incoming incomplete letter, four long surviving blocks. Explicitly answers unlocated Darwin questions about Cape mountain vegetation and Rubus distribution. Separates Zeyher reported observations, Bunbury personal recollections, estimated elevations, missing surveys, and hypotheses about aridity/wind. Myrsine distribution is a difficulty he judges unresolved under both migration and separate creation; do not convert it into Darwin agreement. Later Darwin cold-period annotations are undated, and later book citations do not establish April receipt. No direct reply or new exact knowledge date identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1763: Additional full reading, October 10 supplied 1855. Mrs Hooker supplies return/move news, not necessarily a Joseph Hooker incoming letter. Seeds from Kew arrived about ten to fourteen days earlier and are distinct from the two Norwegian seeds. Darwin explicitly has the latter and plans ten-day flotation followed by naming and planting at Kew; those stages are not complete on this evidence. Capsicum/celery germinated after 137 days. Glasgow letter remains missing, Gourlie kindness is a remembered event, and Candolle is being read rather than necessarily finished. This proves Crowe seed-shipment information was known by October 10, earlier than the November direct reply.

reading_method: Six targets and extra October 10 Hooker witness independently read in full with original XML date and voice attributes, body prose, exclusions, undated Darwin annotations, complete apparatus and bibliography. No figures.
